learn.title: Telling files about each other
learn.body: A header file ends in `.h`. It lists what a `.c` file offers, so other files can use it. Before calling a function, the compiler needs its name and types.

learn.title: Declaration and definition
learn.body: `int twice(int n);` is a declaration, also called a prototype. It gives the name, parameters and return type. A definition adds the body in braces. A function can be declared many times but defined once.

learn.title: A small header
learn.body: `#ifndef` and `#define` form an include guard: if the header is pasted twice, the second copy is skipped.

learn.title: Angle brackets or quotes
learn.body: Angle brackets, as in `#include` with `stdio.h`, look in the system folders, for standard headers. Quotes, as in `#include "twice.h"`, look in your own folder first, for headers you wrote.

learn.title: Use your own header
steps: Now `main.c` can call `twice`, and the compiler checks the types
The body lives in `twice.c` and the linker joins it later

learn.body: Put declarations in headers and function bodies in `.c` files.

questions.prompt: What does a header mostly contain?
questions.explanation: Headers list names and types. The bodies sit in `.c` files.

questions.prompt: What is `int twice(int n);` called? One word works.
questions.explanation: It declares the function without giving a body, so it is a prototype or declaration.

questions.prompt: Which include is right for a header you wrote yourself?
questions.explanation: Quotes search your own folder first. Angle brackets are for system headers.

questions.prompt: `stdio.h` is included with angle brackets because it is a \_\_ header.
questions.explanation: Standard headers live in the system folders.

questions.prompt: What is an include guard for?
choices: Skipping a header that was already pasted
questions.explanation: `#ifndef` skips the body the second time, so nothing is repeated.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Declarations go in headers, definitions in `.c` files.

questions.prompt: Where should the body of `twice` live?
questions.explanation: Keep bodies in a `.c` file and declarations in the header.
